column1: # Every row is an obligation, not a number: a compound proposition has several rows.
# status: met | owed | ruling-open | outside | field | note
# met: a production path exists, and a test whose own comment says which ruling it is for.
# owed: the ruling is closed and the work is owed - the one status that never closes.

column7: note
closed: authority only from its own causal past; alive: it grows, and reopening does not start over
v1: everything a carrier writes lies in its one directory; removed, the folder is the person's again, untouched
Rokh is complete without a network; no layer of the core brings in a transport
without a ledger nothing is checked at all; a quotation without an address and an outside address are both refused
the authority must be a grant standing in the causal past and the receipt an intent really opened; an ordinary event is neither
a bound program passes its answer through the gate and the ledger judges, not the program itself
v1 (contract C4): the signed head is the one byte string and names its body by hash; a damaged stored record is refused, never served
v1: the ledger compares the bytes under a full name and refuses a second byte string; the collision is seen
a short name lengthens byte by byte until it is unique among the names in view
v1: freshness is tag 0x0009 of the signed head (contract 3.4); two acts are two events, a replay one; a head without it is refused
the same bytes again: without effect, and valid
v1 reads RKH3 only; RKH1 and RKH2 are refused by name, not called malformed, and their bytes are untouched (contract 3.4, section 7)
an old generation is read as long as its verifier is kept
one explicit act, and no other way
the shell: a sentence sits in the working state, the shape of its effect is shown, and `write` closes it
verification is the ceiling of inference; a hidden branch comes to light only with earlier evidence
the least that is needed travels; the rule is closed and built
the name, type and place of the field, order, repetition, the binding to the event: open by ruling 13.1
the receiver holds only the shown part; the owner's audit is another question and a separate function
v1: the footprint is the whole trace, and nothing in it is legible
v1: files are named by place alone, so a full and an empty carrier list alike; a slab moved under another name does not open (contract V3, V4)

v1 keeps no atomic file write: contract C2 (the core never relies on an atomic rename or a directory flush), section 1 (no temporary file, no lock file, no rename) and 2.10 (Medium.Write writes in place). A cut at any byte is carried by the commit point, T8.5/the-point
v1: one recording is one commit whose point is the head file (contract 2.6); cut at any write before it, nothing is recorded and the reopened ledger holds only what the committed references reach
v1 (contract 4.6): the owner's passphrase has no recovery and gets none
v1 profile: one directory of N slab files and four head files (contract section 1), and nothing else
what is seen before closing is a prediction of the effect and has no name
that a sentence can be read aloud and understood is not measured by a machine test
both halves are signed events; the id of the intent is the name of those bytes, and the outcome names it as its parent
a custom, not a law of the core; the import graph is closed downwards
address, verb and the declared type of the payload, all three; never the name
the repeat handle takes hold in this same ledger; four policies are declared in harness.Effects
four separate authorities: none follows from another (12 pairs tested); a shared pen with share, keep and a receipt of return in bond/pen.go
unfinished until root key rotation (13.2) is closed
eight named stages; the bound holds at every stage; the passages deliberately open: Permitted is always ErrCycleOpen
four clauses, and no third answer that guesses
an undeclared verb inside the program's own space gets the answer the program itself declared; the core does not guess
the stamp is inside the signed payload; the version is bound to the event itself
the exact root is the program itself and the receipt shelf; the subtree is the verb space, under 11.10; a receipt below the root is refused, not ignored
intent and outcome are words of the procedure, not verbs of the covenant; declaring them does not close the covenant
a bound program puts its receipt at the root; below it is refused, and the refusal says where the root is
v1: what has not arrived is pending, answered ancestry_unproven, not refused, and accepted once it arrives (contract C8, B8)
the seat of judgement is deliberately empty; an untouched ledger produces nothing
an epistemic bound: no test can prove that the binary that runs is the same code, and a test that claimed it would be exactly the over-claim this band warns against
sealing content for a specific receiver: X25519+HKDF+GCM, and the bundle is closed before it is handed to the courier
the byte form of selective disclosure: ruling open
root key rotation: ruling open
the real folder: one folder per draft, files for address, verb and payload; editing with any tool is rewriting the draft; saving records nothing
a mirror declares its seat; its anchor is read from the carrier's public face, not from its claim, and the two never become one
a mirror is opened and read; any sentence written on it is refused at the door, not after signing
the reader of a bond: still an open ruling
the gate takes the four-clause covenant and holds the program to it
that someone other than us writes is a field test
two real ledgers: each accepts the same name in its own ledger; neither holds the other's event
succession: the passages and the holders of authority are not closed
key recovery: outside the design, by ruling 8.6
a full-name collision: seeing it is closed, what to do is open
one person, offline, verifies the whole ledger; Add is that program, event by event
v1 (contract C4): the head is the one byte string, signed, hashed and stored; changed bytes are never the same event
the same: a connection adds access, not completeness
one content, one encoding: keys sorted, no spaces, explicit escapes; a second spelling is refused, not repaired
v1 profile (contract C3): Ed25519, SHA-256, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, X25519 envelopes, fixed slabs named by place; exercised, not only named
the adversary table: who took the carrier sees a rokh vessel and reads nothing; who holds the passphrase reads everything
a compromised host: the trust boundary lies before Rokh, and Rokh can do nothing about it
the answer is always relative to a point; revocation closes the future, not the past
the ledger attests the author and the order, not the truth
the same bound as T12.6, from the side of open code
the seventeenth minute is not counted
verification in place of the vote, bytes in place of trust, and nothing in the seat of judgement
